pr_title: Fix `DistanceSnapGrid` not applying spacing multiplier appropriately
pr_body:
- Closes #18073 

Was occuring due to the multiplier being applied to the `DistanceSpacing` property only, while everywhere else is unaware of it, and, in return, produce incorrect time/position values.

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22781491/166667014-196b3bbe-322e-48fd-bd16-ef28ae259da9.mp4

Haven't added tests as that'll require a bit of more effort, but can look into it tonight/tomorrow if needed.

@peppy please check that this resolves the issues you have with distance snapping, looks to be all correct now.
pr_comments: Closing in favour of https://github.com/ppy/osu/pull/18103 which resolves the issue by applying the distance spacing to the snapping position logic directly, rather than covering the `DistanceSnapGrid` entirely with the distance spacing in the snap methods.

issue_context.title: Distance snapping looks to be broken
issue_context.body:
### Type

Game behaviour

### Bug description

When set to non-1.0x, the distance snap grid provided snaps do not align correctly:

![osu! 2022-05-03 at 09 26 55](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/191335/166431295-6a55253c-d19c-4051-80d4-92b10abda1b8.png)

As an aside, there's also no way to reset the distance snap to default:

![osu! 2022-05-03 at 09 26 09](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/191335/166431160-a1d7be24-c603-4410-b103-e36362dfd277.png)



### Screenshots or videos

_No response_

### Version

master

### Logs

-
comments:
https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/191335/166431781-18f5fe7e-7ae4-4946-9a87-bd523f9bc280.mp4

I can't explain what's going on, but colours don't match with timeline, and some ticks are skipped at random.

review_comments:
While the implementation looks correct, I believe this is potentially implemented in the wrong place.

Right now, the DI'd `snapProvider` here is `HitObjectComposer` which directly owns the `DistanceSnapGrid`. In other implementations (like https://github.com/ppy/osu/blob/bb086800b1e528205cfcd635c093798bc87e2a0c/osu.Game.Rulesets.Osu/Edit/OsuHitObjectComposer.cs#L142-L143) the application of the grid snap is being done in `HitObjectComposer` itself, and I feel like maybe this should be moved there as well?

The rationale is that other components may call `GetBeatSnapDistanceAt` on their resolved snap provider, which will be the `HitObjectComposer`. I think even in those cases the distance spacing multiplier needs to be accounted for.

Not 100% sure and maybe you'll find a reason it can't be done there, but worth a try (mainly to reduce complexity if it does so).

Well, this was actually how it was done previously, until https://github.com/ppy/osu/pull/16576#discussion_r860450100 in which I realised doing that is actually wrong, because we never want to have the distance spacing applied until we're snapping with the distance grid.

It does mean that `DistanceSpacingMultiplier` is in a completely wrong position, and I'm not entirely sure how that one should be solved. Maybe by resolving "`DistancedHitObjcetComposer`" and calling it a day?
To confirm, you're saying that "the only time we will want to apply distance snapping is when interacting with the distance spacing grid"?
When the distance snap/spacing grid is enabled, correct.

This plays around with math a bit, but the summary of it is that input distances need to have the multipler removed (e.g. `DistanceToDuration`, `GetSnappedDurationFromDistance`), while output distances need to have the multiplier applied (e.g. `DurationToDistance`). And then there's `GetSnappedDistanceFromDistance` which does both.

Not sure if I'm the only one who finds that not obvious, but I don't know how it can be explained in an inline comment either.
Is the interface spec here just because-we-can? Or is it used in some way I can't see?

It's more about that `DistanceSnapGrid` now provides its own snap provider logic which builds over the `HitObjectComposer` one, but with the distance spacing multiplier applied. Could include that as part of the xmldoc.
I get that, but I wanted to confirm that it's not being used for DI or anything. ie. removing it here should have no effect, correct?
